note: The script input buffer bounds are passed into the lexer as the implementation values that delimit tokenization.
The input-controlled current lexer pointer is stored in the lexer state.
The end pointer for the same input buffer is stored in the lexer state.
For the one-byte plus input, the lexer consumes the '+' byte and advances lexer->start to lexer->end.
The consumed '+' selects the multi-character addition-token path while no bytes remain in the input buffer.
The loop guard checks only the multi-token table state and omits the required lexer->start < lexer->end bounds check before inspecting the next input byte.
Because lexer->start equals lexer->end after the final '+', this statement reads one byte past the heap input buffer.
